review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–215) and did not open any related sources. The nearest repetition is in HarmonicAt.add, sub, neg, const_smul and comp_CLM. Each proves ContDiffAt from the matching ContDiffAt lemma. Each then runs `filter_upwards` over a library `laplacian_*_nhds` lemma together with `h.2`, and closes with `simp_all`. Each block is only 2–4 lines, and the real mathematics sits in the existing Laplacian lemmas. A shared helper would be a thin wrapper around that API and would not be clearly easier to read or maintain. The HarmonicOnNhd versions are pointwise lifts of the HarmonicAt versions. The `_iff` lemmas and `harmonicAt_congr_nhds` reuse existing lemmas, and `harmonicAt_congr_nhds` repeats a symmetric two-line step that is too small to extract. I found no nontrivial repeated proof machinery that meets the rubric. The only uncertainty is that I did not check how the Laplacian files are written.
